reviewedContract: The new exact wire comparison applies only to the caller-owned original MCP argument document and its actual MCP.Value re-encoding; it does not replace schema or consent admission.
All existing parsing/schema/consent/metadata-removal API bodies are byte-identical; the new comparison exposes no metadata-removal parameter.

Both parse policies and the comparison policy are checked before parsing. Every conversion, multiplication and addition used for the input-derived budgets is checked; no saturation or unlimited mode is introduced.

The actual pinned JSONLimits.validate independently validates every metric and does not impose a cross-metric minimum that would reject smaller valid wire documents. Addressable capacities remain below Int.max and cumulative quotas below UInt64.max.

Pinned parser input-copy/scanning/string retention and comparison admission/textEquals behavior support the separate finite ledgers and conservative byte-linear allowances. Structural/numeric/key/cancellation quotas stay unchanged.
Cancellation checks remain before, between and after pinned operations. Every field including metadata is compared by the existing exact decimal/scalar implementation.

The 11 new controls retain the original >8 MiB Hebrew/emoji shape, a mutation at its tail, scalar/number/type/metadata/syntax fidelity, original resource limits, cancellation, old 1 MiB boundary and all49 policy fields.
limits: Native Swift compilation, budget sufficiency and all11 test outcomes remain NOT_RUN.
The unchanged original real MCP transport/renderer/store acceptance remains required within its original two-minute ceiling.
The resource formulas bound the three independent JSON ledgers; they are not a process RSS or preexisting Foundation/MCP allocation bound.
